subject: Urgent: Dedicated headroom drain — production latency & token errors
messages:
From: Raj Singh <raj.singh@acme.com>
To: support@redwood.ai; logan.wright@redwood.ai
Cc: sales@acme.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: [URGENT] Prod errors + high 99th latency on dedicated pool

Hi team,

We're seeing sustained 99th-percentile latency jumps and a rising 500-response rate from the model endpoints backed by our reserved pool (dedicated-prod-us-east-1-pool-6). The issue started ~14:40 PDT and has continued with intermittent spikes. Impact: user-facing timeouts on our document-extraction flows and ~2% of requests returning tokenization/runtime errors.

What we've observed:
- 99th-latency from ~350ms -> 3.2s for calls hitting the reserved pool
- Error 500 / token errors: ~1.8% -> 2.4% over the last 45 minutes
- Traffic hasn't materially increased on our side (per our telemetry) — roughly 1.2M tokens/day steady state
- Affected routes: /v1/generate (context lengths frequently >12k tokens)

Attached a small error snippet and a metrics snapshot for the timeframe (acme_error_snippet.txt, pool_metrics_snapshot.csv).

We need an immediate mitigation plan: either a temporary capacity relief, routing to a compatible hosted model, or an explicit rollback of a recent runtime change on your side. This is blocking our nightly batch jobs and causing SLA noise with our customers. Please advise next steps and ETA for a fix.

Raj
Raj Singh
Platform Ops, Acme Corp

Attachments: acme_error_snippet.txt (text), pool_metrics_snapshot.csv (csv)
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai; ben.carter@redwood.ai; irene.choi@redwood.ai; markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: raj.singh@acme.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Prod errors + high 99th latency on dedicated pool

Thanks Raj — we've got eyes on this. Internal triage notes below; I'm pulling SRE and the account team into a quick coordination loop.

Initial asks (immediate):
- @Irene: run the pool heatmap and KV cache miss rate for pool-6 across the last 2 hours. Prioritize per-GPU utilization and pending queue depth.
- @Ben: please prepare a temporary routing policy to shift 15-25% of Acme traffic to the nearest compatible hosted variant (same model family, slightly higher latency expected) and estimate cost delta.
- @Marissa: notify Acme AM and prepare comms for a 30-min maintenance window if we need to evict and rebalance nodes.

Short summary of possible causes (hypothesis):
- Long-context requests causing KV-cache thrashing + oversized batches leading to headroom exhaustion
- Recent auto-scaling threshold change that might delay burst capacity spin-up
- A stuck workload or aggressive quantization fallback creating CPU/GPU pressure

Irene — please share quick findings and a recommended short-term mitigation. I'll coordinate the customer-facing reply once we have a concrete action.

Attachments: initial_troubleshoot_notes.md

— Logan
Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: logan.wright@redwood.ai; ben.carter@redwood.ai; marissa.cole@redwood.ai; markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: raj.singh@acme.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Prod errors + high 99th latency on dedicated pool

Quick triage update — findings below (conservative, based on current metrics):

What I see:
- Per-GPU utilization on pool-6 jumped to 96-100% across 6 nodes at ~14:35 PDT; kernel wait times increased sharply
- KV cache miss-rate rose from ~4% -> 22% on long-context routes (12k+ tokens) — this aligns with I/O amplification and longer per-token service time
- Batch sizes have drifted upward in the last 24 hours (observed several requests coalescing into large batches due to a runtime batching heuristic change rolled earlier this week)

Immediate mitigations I can enact in <10 minutes:
1) Reduce effective max-batch size for pool-6 to a lower ceiling (from 64 -> 24) to reduce headroom churn. Will increase per-token latency slightly but cut timeout errors.
2) Apply a temporary route-sample that diverts 20% of Acme traffic to a hosted fallback (compatible quantized variant) — Ben, you mentioned preparing this; I can flip it once you confirm routing rule.
3) Trigger a short, controlled drain/rebalance on 2 of the hottest nodes to free headroom (risk: small increase in tail latency during drain).

I recommend steps 1 + 2 now, step 3 if metrics do not improve in 15 minutes.

Operational notes:
- Console link: https://redwood.app/console/pools/dedicated-prod-us-east-1-pool-6 (live)
- Runbook: https://redwood.app/runbooks/capacity-drain

I'll apply the batch-size change now and report back with 5-min cadence.

— Irene
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Singh <raj.singh@acme.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai; ben.carter@redwood.ai; irene.choi@redwood.ai; markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 17:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Prod errors + high 99th latency on dedicated pool

Raj — thanks for the report and for bearing with us. Here's the short-term plan we're executing immediately:

1) Apply immediate throttling on max-batch size for dedicated-prod-us-east-1-pool-6 (64 -> 24) — expected outcome: reduce headroom thrash and drop token errors; possible small increase in median latency but major reduction in 99th tail.
2) Divert 20% of Acme traffic to a hosted compatible variant (same model family) for the next 2 hours while we stabilize. Expected customer impact: a ~150-300ms increase on rerouted requests; should eliminate the 500 errors for diverted traffic.
3) Run a controlled rebalance on two overloaded nodes during low-traffic window (T+45 min). Will monitor closely; rollback if customer impact increases.

We are also preparing a formal SLA-exception request and a post-incident capacity-sizing changelist (will send within 24 hours). Attached: sla-exception-request.pdf (for Acme procurement / finance reference).

Please confirm if we have permission to proceed with the diversion and the rebalance window at 18:05 PDT. If you prefer a different time, tell us and we'll adjust.

Best,
Logan
Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Raj Singh <raj.singh@acme.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: elena.gomez@fastbank.com; sales@acme.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Prod errors + high 99th latency on dedicated pool

Logan — please proceed with the diversion and the rebalance at 18:05 PDT. We approve the short-term mitigation.

Two asks from our side:
- Please share a short post-action summary and the root-cause hypothesis once you have it.
- We need an impact estimate for the diversion (expected % of user requests that will see increased latency) to share with our PMs.

Copying our SRE lead Elena for visibility. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Raj
Platform Ops, Acme Corp
